nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What type of surveillance is mentioned as being conducted in many protected areas of the Madeira Archipelago?
nodes.answer: Many protected areas in the Madeira Archipelago had permanent surveillance.
nodes.paragraph: 2022). One of the actions of such a plan was to establish a more extensive EU-wide network of protected areas on land and at sea. In the marine realm, EU member states must classify 30% of their national maritime space as marine protected areas (MPAs) by 2030. From a conservation point of Refining management strategies in marine protected areas in oceanic islands: a non indigenous 89 Vol. : (123456789) view, MPAs have been considered a practical instru- ment, namely by promoting the increase in biomass, density, abundance, species richness, and specimens size (e.g., Garc a-Rubies and Zabala 1990; Roberts 1995; Rius 2007). The designation of MPAs has been proposed as a management tool to effectively contrib- ute to the sustainable exploitation of marine resources (e.g., Plan Development Team 1990; Allison et al. 1998; Pauly et al. 2002). Madeira region has been pioneering the creation and implementation of MPAs since the Selvagens Islands Nature Reserve in 1971 (Friedlander et al. 2017). Over the following 50 years, several other protected areas were established in the Madeira Archipelago, many of which had permanent surveil- lance.
